A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CogNav, and all 11 pages of each are readable, including figures, tables, equations, algorithms, and references. Neither contains appendices or embedded supplements. Separately referenced supplementary material is unavailable and is not treated as inspected evidence.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original HM3D and MP3D navigation results, cognitive-state and prompt ablations, alternative language-model experiments, and a real-robot navigation example.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original HM3D, MP3D, and RoboTHOR results, state and prompt ablations, cognitive-state analyses, and a real-robot navigation example.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the specified third occupancy-map channel from unexplored areas to agent location. Algorithm 1 changes OT/CV landmark selectors from VLM to LLM, although v1's prose already described LLM planning. These are limited revisions to the method specification; the five states and overall mapping, prompting, and planning pipeline remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluated RoboTHOR coverage, comprising 15 validation environments and 12 target categories, alongside retained HM3D and MP3D coverage. This substantially broadens the environments represented in the benchmark evaluation. Figure 5 retains the existing simulated plant-search and real-world cup-search examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes OSGs-OWNav, the strongest HM3D comparator in v1 at 69.3% SR and 28.3% SPL. Conversely, v2 Table 3 adds L3MVN, SG-Nav, and TriHelper to the cognitive-state comparison, which previously contained only CogNav variants. These changes materially revise comparator participation.

E3.justification: V2 introduces the RoboTHOR validation setup with 1.8K episodes and adds state-ratio entropy as an analysis metric. The alternative Llama3.1-8B/CogVLM2-19B configuration study disappears. Reported HM3D/MP3D splits, episode counts, 500-step budget, sensor/action settings, and SR/SPL/DTG metrics remain unchanged; score revisions do not establish changed protocols or reruns.

E4.justification: V1's entire LLM/VLM replacement study in Table 5 is absent from v2. V2 expands Figure 6 from sofa/plant state-ratio heatmaps to six-category heatmaps plus entropy analysis for sofa, TV, and plant, and adds external-method context to the state ablation. State-removal and prompt-removal questions otherwise remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's state-ratio entropy describes variability in navigation states, rather than uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces CogNav's HM3D SR/SPL of 87.2/30.4 with 72.5/26.2 and MP3D's 61.1/20.1 with 46.6/16.1; RoboTHOR's 54.6/24.3 is new. Tables 2–4 extensively revise category and ablation values, including some baseline category scores. V1 Table 5 results disappear. The PDFs do not explain the replacements, so they do not establish a verified implementation-level performance regression.

T1.justification: V2 adds Equations (1)–(2) expressing the already described three-part cognitive map and two-part prompting scheme. These restate existing content mathematically; no substantive theoretical assumptions, propositions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The headline empirical claim is substantially revised: v1 reports SR margins of 17.9 percentage points on HM3D and 20.9 on MP3D; v2 reports 10.5 and 6.4, adds 7.1 on RoboTHOR, and summarizes this as at least 14% relative improvement. V2 also withdraws the first-attempt novelty claim while retaining the cognitive-map and five-state contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking cross-method state comparisons to finer cognitive modeling and more effective map prompting, and connects irregular state transitions with longer searches. It removes the interpretation of GPT versus open-model reasoning capabilities. The verification/path-length tradeoff and the stated detection and language-input limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 identifies a custom-built mobile robot and a Unitree quadruped, whereas v1 mentions one unspecified robot. Exact alternative-model identifiers disappear with Table 5, and the planned code/data release statement is removed. The homepage and main implementation settings remain; neither PDF establishes an actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises positioning around coarse two-state and threshold-driven approaches, explicitly contrasts CogNav with SG-Nav, and explains its relationship to scene-graph and Voronoi representations. Added works include MapGPT, NavGPT, Stubborn, Segment Anything, Grounding DINO, and RoboTHOR; removed works include Llama 3, CogVLM2, and OVExp. This exceeds bibliographic renumbering or section relocation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial portions of Section 3.3 are rewritten. Scene-representation discussion is integrated into the LLM-related-work subsection, while state transitions and navigation strategies receive separate explanations. Notation, pseudocode, terminology, and affiliation text are also refined.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 receive revised diagrams and labels. Figure 6 is redesigned and relocated, replacing two normalized-time heatmaps with an entropy chart and six step-based heatmaps. Table 1 gains RoboTHOR columns, Table 3 gains method labels and grouped comparison rows, and Table 5 disappears. Figure 4's caption is shortened.

improvement.justification: V2 improves explanatory clarity and adds RoboTHOR coverage and richer state analyses. However, it removes the strongest v1 HM3D comparator and the model-dependence study, while leaving widespread score replacements unexplained. It also introduces a discrepancy: Section 4.4 claims a 7.8-point SPL increase without candidate verification, whereas Table 3 gives 33.6 minus 26.2, or 7.4. The gains and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
